Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int solve(int n, int e, int d)
{
    if(n==0)return -1;
    if(e==0 || d==0)return 0;
    if(n*6<e*7)return -1;
    if(d<7) return ((d*e)%n==0)? d*e/n : d*e/n +1;
    
    int ans=0;
    
    // complete weeks
    
    int weeks=d/7;
    
    ans+= ((weeks*e*7)% n == 0)? ((weeks*e*7)/n) : ((weeks*e*7)/n)+1 ;
    
    int left = ans*n - weeks*e*7;
    
    // remaining days
    
    int days= d%7;
    
    int req=(days*e-left);
    
    ans+= (req%n == 0 )? (req/n): (req/n)+1;
    return ans;
    
}

int main() {
    int n,e,d;
    cin>>n>>e>>d;
    cout<<solve(n,e,d);
    return 0;
}
